corrections.source_says: The exclusions field should describe the documented post-assignment filtering: sketches from two HAI teams combined multiple ideas on one screen; another pair was removed because its members knew each other, often solved problems together, and had expert design experience. Duplicate screenshots and test marks were also excluded, and common or nonsensical ideas were set aside from the main rated subset. The paper reports 263 sketches initially, 216 after removing the team categories, and 122 sketches from 31 people in the main evaluation; these are different analysis sets, not participant counts that can be interchanged.
corrections.quote: Sketches from two HAI teams could not be evaluated the same way as the others, as they had sketched complex ideas by combining more than one idea on the same screen.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 8, Sections 3.4, 4 and 4.2; p. 10, continuation of Section 4.2; p. 15, Section 5; p. 17, Section 6.3 and Table 8

corrections.source_says: For the sketches-per-team outcome, n_units is 21 and unit remains team. This is the number of teams in the fluency analysis, not the number of people; the person counts remain 35 assigned and 31 retained as separately reported.
corrections.quote: Each of the 21 teams produced from 6 sketches to 23 sketches, as shown in Figure 10.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 4.5; p. 11, Figure 10; p. 12, Table 5; person counts: p. 6, Section 3.2 and p. 15, Section 5

corrections.form_value: No separate usefulness outcome; only the unspecified quality tests, highest novelty ratings, and sketch counts are listed.
corrections.source_says: Add the independently scored usefulness outcome (construct usefulness; measure human_raters). The scale is 1 to 4, with zero for nonsensical sketches. Section 5 reports 4 sketches receiving a usefulness rating of 4; Section 6.3/Table 8 instead reports 9 occurrences of a usefulness rating of 4 (2%) among 216 evaluated sketches. The paper does not reconcile these counts; distinguish sketches from rating occurrences and do not infer an arm mean or effect.
corrections.quote: Only 4 sketches received a rating of 4 on “usefulness,” and none of them received a 3 or 4 rating on novelty
corrections.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 4.3; p. 16, Section 5; p. 17, Section 6.3 and Table 8

corrections.form_value: No variety or flexibility outcome is listed.
corrections.source_says: Add the stated measure of categories represented within each team as flexibility (measure category_count; unit team), not diversity across people. No numerical HH-versus-HAI result for this metric is reported. Preserve the category-count inconsistency: the continuation of Section 4.2 describes 16 groups, comprising 9 toddler and 7 computer groups, whereas Section 4.5 specifies 9 and 6; do not resolve it by guessing.
corrections.quote: Variety based on how many of the identified groups (9 groups in the first task and 6 in the second) were represented in a team’s ideas
corrections.locator: PDF p. 10, continuation of Section 4.2 and Section 4.5, item 6

corrections.source_says: Document the two trained research assistants and their separate usefulness and novelty ratings: scores 1 to 4, with zero for ideas judged not useful or not novel. The retained 122 sketches yield 488 ratings across the two aspects and two raters. These output and rating counts should not be substituted for people, and this description does not resolve the unspecified aggregation or analysis unit used in Table 6.
corrections.quote: For the 122 sketches and 2 raters assigning values for novelty and usefulness, 488 distinct scores emerge.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 3.2; p. 10, Section 4.3; p. 12, Section 4.6; p. 15, Section 4.8/Table 6

corrections.form_value: All three outcomes have empty ai_available_when_produced and timing strings.
corrections.source_says: The scored sketches were produced during the experimental tasks, so timing is immediate. For the HAI treatment outputs, the described AI aid was available during production (yes); HH participants had the suggestion feature disabled. This describes availability of the retrieval aid and does not establish that it was generative AI. No later unaided assessment is reported.
corrections.quote: a tablet with the presence of an AI assistant in the background for HAI teams or a disabled AI for HH teams.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 7, Sections 3.2-3.3 and Table 3; p. 10, Section 4.5

corrections.form_value: All three contrasts have empty treatment_arm, control_arm, comparison_type and direction; statistics_available is also empty.
corrections.source_says: Identify Human-AI (HAI) as treatment and Human-human (HH) as control. The comparator is an active human partner (comparison_type ai_vs_active), and all three printed contrasts favor HAI (direction treatment_higher), subject to the existing reporting caveats. For S1-O1, statistics_available should include test_statistic because Table 6 supplies t statistics and p values; S1-O3 also has reported arm means and SDs, with teams as the observation unit. This comparison coding does not override the unresolved generative-AI qualification.
corrections.quote: Table 6 shows the results from using the Python function: stats.ttest_ind (HAI, HH, equal_var=False).
corrections.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract; p. 7, Table 3; p. 12, Table 5; p. 15, Section 4.8/Table 6; p. 16, Section 5/Table 7

corrections.source_says: The paper explicitly supplies the data URL https://github.com/makokhamj/H-AI-Study. Record this as the stated data location; the repository contents were not independently checked, and the statement does not establish a separate code URL.
corrections.quote: The data that support the findings of this study are openly available at https://github.com/makokhamj/H-AI-Study.

confirmed: The source is the journal research article by Joseph M. Makokha, published online 28 May 2026 in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 00(00), with 22 PDF pages; the recorded title and version match (PDF p. 1 and PDF page count). The complete markdown, including the end matter and references, was read; no appendix or separately cited supplement was identified.

Random assignment of 35 senior undergraduate and beginning graduate students to HH or HAI teams is explicit; the supervised university research setting supports lab_rct (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2; p. 7, Section 3.3).

The false has_randomized_people_study flag refers specifically to the absence of confirmed generative-AI assistance, not to absence of random assignment: the implementation matches sketches to existing images and returns library suggestions through a ResNet-50 classifier, despite the author calling it generative elsewhere (PDF p. 2, Section 2.1; pp. 4-5, Section 2.4; pp. 5-6, Sections 3.1-3.1.3). Retaining criterion_1 as unclear is justified by this conflict.

The main evaluation explicitly retains 122 sketches from 31 participants; 263 in Table 6 is an idea count, not a people count (PDF p. 15, Sections 4.8 and 5, Table 6). Arm-specific randomized and analyzed people counts are not explicitly reported, so the form appropriately leaves them null (PDF pp. 6-8, methods; pp. 10-17, results).

Core=no, criterion_2=not_met and context_class=none are supported: the study has fewer than 50 analyzed people and is a small randomized collaboration experiment, rather than an observational, AI-versus-human-output or synthesis context study (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 3.2-3.3; p. 15, Section 5; codebook Sections 3-4).

The tasks were getting a toddler into bed and transporting a computer on campus, with two consecutive approximately 7-minute sketching tasks and the AI feature disabled for HH (PDF p. 7, Sections 3.2-3.3 and Table 3).

S1-O1 reported statistics are exact: All ideas (263), t=3.814, p=0.00014; Highly rated (122), t=2.773, p=0.00729; equal_var=False (PDF p. 15, Section 4.8 and Table 6). The following prose incorrectly calls the t statistics means, and the score aggregation and analysis unit remain unspecified, as the form cautions.

S1-O2 reproduces the printed counts: HAI 17 versus HH 5 with at least one rating of 4, and HAI 8 versus HH 2 with ratings of 4 from both raters (PDF p. 16, Section 5 and Table 7). Table 7 repeats sketch IDs 25, 126, 129 and 212, while Section 6.3 reuses 17 versus 5 under the different average-rating cutoff of 4.0 or 3.5; the form correctly flags these inconsistencies (PDF pp. 16-17).

S1-O3 and the one-line finding correctly report HAI mean 11.9, SD 5.8 versus HH mean 8.5, SD 3.2, as sketches per team (PDF p. 12, Table 5); the separately stated 31 retained participants is also exact (PDF p. 15, Section 5).

This is not a synthesis and supplies no pooled meta-analytic estimates; the synthesis defaults are appropriate. The classifier-validation exercise uses a subset of sketches from this study and is not another randomized people experiment (PDF p. 10, Section 4.4; pp. 6-17, methods and results).
summary: The PDF confirms random assignment of 35 people and retention of 31, but the documented system retrieves existing images and does not establish an in-scope generative-AI experiment. The reported numerical results match the PDF; corrections concern omitted exclusions, outcomes, analysis metadata, and the data URL.
